text:
Ava (Head of Product): quick follow-up from today's all-hands re: packaging + usage policy. drop short Qs about credits, escalation paths, and what to tell customers. we'll capture into a single FAQ.

Rory (Customer Success): customer asked: if they request an emergency credit lift for a launch, how fast can we respond and what info do we need?

Mike (Billing PM): hosted: self-serve temporary burst is immediate if payment method on file. for manual emergency lifts we need account id, proposed amount, launch window, and a contact. typical SLA: 1-2 hours for verification. Dedicated/Private: CS+Finance coordination, target 4 hours.

Jules (Finance): what docs do we need for contractual temporary increases (for invoicing)?

Mike (Billing PM): we need email approval from admin + ticket record. finance will issue a short amendment for reserves > $10k. smaller bursts documented in ticket and invoice.

Nina (Eng Ops): technical note: top-ups propagate in ~60-90s. advise customers to apply jumps a minute before traffic changes. transient 429s can occur during propagation.

Rory (Customer Success): customers want a canned message to use with their stakeholders when a soft-degrade happens. can we produce a 1-paragraph template?

Ava (Head of Product): yes, we'll draft a short template. Mike, can you also add a checklist for self-serve burst vs manual request?

Mike (Billing PM): will do. checklist: payment method? desired units? duration? priority contact? verify region & quotas.

quota-bot: pinned note: /docs/usage/credits-escalation.md

Ava (Head of Product): action items: Mike drafts escalation checklist + one-paragraph customer template, Nina adds propagation note to rate-limit doc, Rory to collect 3 customer examples of launch needs. publish FAQ end of week.

Rory (Customer Success): collecting examples now. thanks — will DM if more nuance. :thumbsup:

Ava (Head of Product): closing in 24h unless there are follow-ups. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
